question: Why is a Random Blood Sugar (RBS) test so handy in everyday clinic or ward work?

options.A: It provides a three-month average of blood sugar
options.B: It is completely painless for every patient
options.C: It does not require a drop of blood
options.D: It can be done at any time without fasting

explanation: You don't need your patient to fast beforehand! That makes RBS a lifesaver during busy shifts and emergency admissions when you need answers right away.

question: In a busy emergency unit, why do nurses grab the glucometer so quickly?

options.A: It stops the liver from making extra glucose
options.B: It proves whether the patient has diabetes permanently
options.C: It replaces the need for a full medical history
options.D: It helps spot dangerous high or low sugar levels fast

explanation: Portable glucometers give you results in seconds. Catching a dangerously high or low blood sugar early lets you step in and save the day!

question: A patient's blood sugar drops suddenly. Which classic signs will you likely see first?
explanation: When blood sugar crashes, the body sounds an internal alarm (the sympathetic nervous system), making the patient shaky, sweaty, and jittery. Keep some juice nearby!

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency ward. What is one of the quickest bedside checks you should do?
explanation: Always check blood sugar when a patient's mental status changes. It takes seconds to rule out severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia, which can look just like confusion!

question: What happens if glucometer test strips are left open to air and moisture for too long?

options.A: The chemical reagents inside them get ruined
options.B: They turn into a liquid gel substance
options.C: They change color to bright neon green
options.D: They become completely sterile to touch

explanation: Test strips are delicate! Moisture and air mess up the sensitive chemicals inside, giving you false readings. Always snap that strip container lid tightly shut.

question: Why must you check the expiration date on the test strip bottle before testing a patient?

options.A: Expired strips will refuse to fit into the meter
options.B: The glucometer automatically locks out expired strips
options.C: Using expired strips violates hospital electricity codes
options.D: Expired strips may give incorrect readings

explanation: The chemicals on strips degrade as time passes. Using fresh strips means you can trust your numbers and give safe patient care.

question: After pricking a finger for blood sugar, why should you wipe away the very first drop?

options.A: It contains tissue fluid that can dilute the sample
options.B: The glucometer machine will reject the first drop
options.C: It prevents the puncture site from bruising
options.D: It is contaminated with dangerous skin bacteria

explanation: That initial droplet usually mixes with clear tissue fluid from the skin poke, which throws off the glucose reading. Wiping it away gives you a true blood sample!

question: What is the right step after cleaning a patient's fingertip with an alcohol swab?

options.A: Wait for the alcohol to dry completely on the skin
options.B: Blow on the finger to speed up the drying process
options.C: Wipe the wet alcohol off with a sterile gauze pad
options.D: Prick the wet finger immediately to save time

explanation: If the alcohol is still wet, it mixes with the blood drop and dilutes it, giving you a false reading. A few seconds of patience guarantees an accurate result!

question: Along with classic symptoms, what random blood sugar level usually points toward diabetes?
explanation: An RBS reading of 200 mg/dL or more, paired with signs like extreme thirst and frequent urination, is a strong red flag for diabetes.

question: Why can't a nurse officially diagnose a patient with diabetes based on just one high random blood sugar test?

options.A: Glucometers cannot measure glucose above 150 mg/dL
options.B: Blood sugar levels never stay high for long periods
options.C: It is a screening test and needs confirmatory tests
options.D: Only laboratory nurses are allowed to make a diagnosis

explanation: Meals, stress, and illness can cause temporary spikes. Doctors rely on fasting tests or HbA1c to make a formal diagnosis.

question: Why might a patient with a severe infection show high blood sugar even if they haven't eaten?

options.A: Fever causes the glucometer to malfunction permanently
options.B: White blood cells consume all the insulin in the body
options.C: Infections directly damage the beta cells in the kidneys
options.D: Stress hormones released during illness raise blood sugar

explanation: When the body fights severe stress or infection, hormones like adrenaline and cortisol surge, telling the liver to dump extra glucose into the blood.

question: Which common class of medications is well known for pushing a patient's blood sugar up?
explanation: Drugs like prednisolone make the body less sensitive to insulin and push the liver to make more sugar. Good to watch out for in clinical practice!

question: A conscious patient's random blood sugar is 52 mg/dL and they feel shaky. What should you do right away?

options.A: Give 15 grams of fast-acting oral carbohydrates
options.B: Send the patient for an emergency CT scan of the head
options.C: Inject long-acting insulin into the deltoid muscle
options.D: Wait patiently for two hours and test the blood again

explanation: Since the patient is awake and able to swallow, give them quick-acting sugar (like glucose tablets or juice) to bring their blood sugar back up safely.

question: Why is it dangerous to give sugary drinks to an unconscious patient with low blood sugar?

options.A: The stomach will reject all sugary liquids
options.B: It can cause choking or enter the lungs
options.C: It will immediately cause a diabetic coma
options.D: It takes three days for the body to digest it

explanation: An unconscious patient cannot protect their airway. Giving them fluids by mouth can cause aspiration, sending liquid straight into their lungs. Safety first!

question: What is a vital safety item a patient living with diabetes should always carry around?

options.A: An extra pair of clean examination gloves
options.B: A spare blood pressure cuff and stethoscope
options.C: A quick source of sugar like glucose tablets
options.D: A bottle of surgical rubbing alcohol

explanation: Hypoglycemia can strike anywhere. Having glucose tablets or sweets on hand lets the patient treat a sudden crash immediately.

question: Why is washing hands with soap and water so important before a home blood glucose test?

options.A: Soap adds essential vitamins into the skin capillaries
options.B: Food residue on fingers can falsely raise the reading
options.C: Water activates the electronic screen on the meter
options.D: It is the only way to sterilize the testing strip

explanation: If a patient just ate fruit or biscuits, sticky sugar residue on their fingers will mix with the blood droplet and give a falsely high reading. Clean hands mean honest numbers!
